## Calculator skills · enter values and frequencies {#l2-calculator .compact}

::: {.split}
::: {.column-block}

| $x$ | Frequency |
|:---:|:---:|
| 0 | 15 |
| 1 | 20 |
| 2 | 10 |
| 3 | 4 |
| 4 | 1 |

<a class="calculator-link" href="https://classpad.net/note/#/tools/math" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open calculator demonstration ↗</a>

:::
::: {.column-block}

1. Open **Statistics → 1-Variable**.
2. Set **TOOLS → Frequency → On** before entering data.
3. Enter the values in **x** and their counts in **Freq**.
4. Open **1-Var Results** and check **n = 50**.
5. Read the mean, median, quartiles, minimum and maximum.

```{=html}
<div data-module="reveal-panel" class="calculator-check"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show check values</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><p><span data-math="\bar{x}=1.12">mean = 1.12</span>; median = 1</p><p><span data-math="Q_1=0,\quad Q_3=2">Q₁ = 0, Q₃ = 2</span>; min = 0, max = 4</p><p>Range = 4; IQR = 2; mode = 1</p></div></div>
```

:::
:::

<p class="small-note">Calculate range = max − min and IQR = <span data-math="Q_3-Q_1">Q₃ − Q₁</span>. Read the mode from the table.</p>

::: notes
Model live using the user's ClassPad.net tool and the ClassWiz interface shown in their screenshot. Open the external calculator in a new tab so the lesson retains its state. Turn Frequency On before entering data: changing this setting clears the data on the fx-8200 AU. Enter f, not cf, rf or fx, into Freq. If n=5 instead of50, frequencies have not been entered correctly. Check the weighted total Σx=56 if displaying summations; the calculator's Σx includes the frequency weights and equals our table's Σfx.

Students follow on their own calculators. Retrieve mean, median and five-number summary; calculate range and IQR separately. Mode is read from the frequency table. Other calculator models may use different menu labels.

Menu sequence checked against the official Casio fx-8200 AU manual: https://support.casio.com/global/en/calc/manual/fx-8200AU_en/using_calculator_apps/statistical_calculations.html . Do not extend into variance or standard deviation in this lesson.
:::
